source_text: ἀποστολὴ, πλὴν εἰς βασιλείαν καὶ δόξαν. Τελειοῖ γὰρ οὕτως τὸν Ἀαρὼν, χρυσοῦν ἐπὶ τῷ μετώπῳ τὸ ψαλίον τιθείς. Κύριος δὲ τῶν ὅλων καὶ βασιλεὺς, ὁ Χριστὸς, φυσικῶς τε ἅμα καὶ μεθεκτῶς. Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν φύσει κεκένωκεν ἑαυτὸν, καθεὶς ἐν δούλου μορφῇ
pass_a_gloss: …mitra hyakinthos… basileia ouk ek kosmou… ekenōsen heauton…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …sending, yet unto kingdom and glory. For thus he perfects Aaron, setting the golden plate upon the forehead. And Lord of the wholes and king is Christ, both naturally together and by participation. For being God by nature he has emptied himself, having come down in a slave’s form. And he receives kingdom, according at least to what is fitting for the human shape, though from above and from beginning sitting-with God and Father, and co-ruling the wholes and co-master. And understand how from hyacinth his mitre has come to be, having the bright signal of the kingdom—I mean the golden leaf. And hyacinth is a sign of heaven; and remember Christ saying, ‘My kingdom is not from this world.’ (Exodus 28:38) For not an earthly king, but heavenly is Christ, having all the creation under feet. And having added, that ‘And Aaron will take away the sins of the holy things, as many as they should sanctify, of every gift of their holy things,’ (Philippians 2:7) that every approach and perfection is in Christ, he has made clear… And Christ ‘in a hidden hand,’ (Psalm 7:12–13) according to what has been written, and ‘His bow he has stretched, and prepared it, his arrows for those being burned he has worked out,’ (John 18:36) and he has taken down rulers, has triumphed over powers, has shaken lordships, and has rescued those upon the earth being captives. And that the war has not become visible or thick for him, nor such as toward blood and flesh, the warlike gear having come to be from linen alone the very (Ephesians 6:12) (Colossians 2:15)
